provenance.prompt:
J.113 / Piper Quickstep — FALL action sheet, attempt 1

Create one original production sprite sheet for Piper Quickstep performing a controlled, nonviolent basketball fall and recovery. Use the supplied accepted Piper sheets only as identity, anatomy, uniform and rendering references; do not copy their poses. Piper is an adult athletic human woman with warm-brown skin, expressive brown eyes, a bright orange high ponytail tied behind her head, a russet-red sleeveless basketball jersey and shorts with cream/white piping and paired cream side stripes, white socks, and red/cream high-top trainers. Preserve her face, hair, skin tone, natural athletic proportions, complete human anatomy and exact uniform palette. Keep the uniform completely blank: no text, numbers, logos, jewelry or added marks. She has exactly two arms with two natural hands, five fingers per hand, two legs and two shoes. Keep all hands visibly empty.

Canvas and grid: genuine transparent RGBA, exactly 1536×1024 pixels. Arrange exactly ten separate complete right-facing three-quarter poses in a precise 5-column × 2-row row-major grid, one Piper in each cell. Five columns divide the width into equal nominal cells; two rows are 512 pixels each. Keep every full figure, including all ponytail strands, fingertips and both shoes, at least 60 pixels inside every source-cell boundary. Keep one consistent figure scale and clear gutters; silhouettes must not touch, overlap, merge, cross a cell edge, or touch the canvas boundary. Keep alpha zero everywhere outside the figures. Do not draw cell dividers.

Exact ten-pose nonviolent controlled fall sequence, in row-major order. The finish anchor is frame 9 at simulation tick 33; frame durations are [2,2,2,3,3,4,5,6,6,7], so frame starts are ticks [0,2,4,6,9,12,16,21,27,33].
0. Finish a disrupted balance step, torso starting to tip while both empty hands open for balance.
1. Stumble forward with one foot catching late, shoulders uneven and arms spread.
2. Lower the center of gravity, bend the knees and reach one open hand down to brace.
3. One knee reaches the floor first while the opposite palm supports her; keep the second hand visible and empty.
4. Controlled sideways descent onto one hip, with legs bent safely and ponytail flowing behind.
5. Settle on her side with one palm supporting her weight; do not hide either arm or shoe.
6. Seated recovery on one hip, one hand planted and the other open near her torso.
7. Turn onto one knee and plant a hand to push upward.
8. Rise into a low crouch with both feet under her and hands returning to a defensive guard.
9. Finish fully upright in a balanced ready stance at simulation tick 33, looking alert and uninjured.

Show only Piper in all ten cells. The basketball remains a separate game object and must not appear in the athlete art. No ball, sphere, seams, opponent, teammate, hoop, rim, court, floor, ground shadow, glow, speed lines, impact star, dust, scenery, background color, checkerboard, grid, dividers, border, text, logo, number, prop or UI. Preserve true alpha-zero background and gutters. Return only the complete sprite sheet.
